newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle surge to new highs at close.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle surge to new highs at close.

text.p: CME feeder cattle futures surged to new contract highs following the May expiration at midday Thursday on expectations of strong cash markets going into the fall and on buy stops, traders said.

Feeder cattle closed 0.775 to 0.100 cent per lb higher paced by August at 78.425 cents. August also set a new high of 78.500 cents. September and January also set new highs. May expired earlier at 76.275 cents, off 0.400 cent for the day.
Live cattle ended 0.100 to 0.325 cent per lb higher with June up the least at 65.325 cents. December posted a new contract high of 71.375 cents.

Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst for Dean Witter, cited expectations of strength in fed cattle and lower feed costs going into the fall which will keep demand for feeders strong.

"Everything in the cash (feeders) is being priced higher and higher into the fall delivery time period. When it comes to yearlings, it is going to be hard to find them in the spot market come October -- everything I know of is being contracted," Benson said.
May kept in line with the index ahead of expiration with rolling of longs adding to pressure there, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index slipped $0.02 lower to $76.35 per cwt. The final index for cash settlement of the May contract is expected to be between $76.10 and $76.30, floor sources said.
Dean Witter actively bought August early. Locals sold before turning buyers late along with Smith Barney. Refco bought August and sold May early, pit sources said.

Deferred months of live cattle paced the advance there with expectations of lighter fed cattle supplies later in the year providing the bulk of support. Nearbys followed on light speculative and technical buying, traders said.

There will be less cattle going on feed as feeder cattle supplies tighten by the third quarter. The active placements that took place earlier this year will be sold off and fed supplies will trend lower, they said.
Technical support followed the futures runup after holding support near the 40-day average in June on Wednesday.

Longs and shorts alike rolled positions into August which made for uneven trade at times. Cargill Investor Services continued to buy August late while R.J. O'Brien sold. Cargill was on both sides of August and also spread long December and February live cattle/short August feeders, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commercials sold June 65 puts and 65 calls while doing the August 64'66 risk reversal. Commission houses bought December 74 and 76 calls. Volatility remained low at nine percent, pit sources added.
